title: Graceful degradation and circuit fallback strategies for post-ranking service
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: The post-ranking endpoint (used by search and recommendation pipelines) is a high-cost, latency-sensitive stage which has recently shown cascading failures under cross-region load spikes. Customer-facing consequences include increased p95 latency, requests hitting timeouts, and elevated fallback rates that degrade result quality.

Goal: Implement a health-aware, SLO-driven degradation strategy for the post-ranking service that combines dynamic timeouts, circuit breakers per-region and per-tenant, and configurable fallback profiles (cached-local, approximate-similarity, and degraded-model variants). The aim is to preserve availability and latency SLOs while minimizing customer-visible quality loss during capacity constraints or infra incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic routed away from unhealthy regions within 30s of health deterioration according to the new region_health_score metric
Per-tenant circuit breaker trips isolate noisy customers and reduce error propagation (observed reduction in global p95 by >= 10% under induced noise)
Dynamic timeout layer enforces max end-to-end deadline and gracefully falls back to cheaper ranking variants without increasing 500 error rate
Fallback rate, quality delta (MRR/CTR), and cost-per-1k metrics are visible in console dashboards and regressions are alerted
Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic with guardrails and automated rollback on quality or SLO regressions
design_notes: Region health score: combine node-level CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, per-node latency p95, and recent error rate into a single 0-100 score. Primary decisions will use thresholds (healthy >= 70, degraded 40-69, unhealthy < 40).

Circuit breakers: implement hierarchical breakers - global service-level, region-level, and tenant-level. Use sliding windows with exponential backoff for reset. Persist breaker state in the control plane to enable cross-instance coordination.

Timeout semantics: introduce two timeouts - a controller timeout (short) for routing/health checks and an endpoint deadline (longer) for model inference. Endpoint deadline enforces a fallback pipeline if not met (e.g., return cached ranking or approximate scorer).

Fallback profiles: define a profile catalog (quality-first, latency-first, cost-first). Profiles map to a prioritized list of fallback chains: 1) local in-memory cache hit, 2) small-probe approximate model (quantized, CPU-friendly), 3) coarse embedding-sim similarity with cheap approximate nearest neighbors, 4) last-known-good ranking (stale but fast).
Admission control: integrate with existing admission controller to limit concurrency per-tenant and queue requests with priority for SLO-backed customers.

Routing: smart routing policy will prefer local region, but will route to adjacent region with healthy score >= 70; otherwise degrade using local fallbacks. Prefer region with lowest expected cost given current queueing projection.
implementation_tasks: Add region_health_score aggregation and expose via control plane telemetry API (ENG: infra + runtime)
Implement hierarchical circuit breaker middleware in post-ranking gateway with persisted state storage
Add dynamic timeout and fallback handler in the post-ranking service; implement fallback catalog and hooks for cheap-scorers
Wire fallback profiles into per-tenant config (console + API) with safe defaults
Extend admission controller to accept profile weights and tenant priorities
Build canary/feature flagging around new routing and breaker logic (launchdarkly + internal flags)
Create automated chaos test harness to simulate region degradations and noisy tenants
Add dashboards and SLI/SLO alerts: p50/p95 latency, fallback rate, breaker trips, regional health changes, MRR drop for a representative prompt set
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): unit tests and local integration using mock health metrics
Stage 2 (staging): run with synthetic traffic and chaos tests; verify fallbacks and breaker behaviour
Stage 3 (canary): 5% of production traffic for low-risk tenants (non-paying/low SLA) for 48 hours
Stage 4 (ramped canary): 20% with automated checks for 7 days; measure quality and SLOs
Stage 5 (ga): enable for all tenants with default profile; provide opt-out and per-tenant tuning via console
monitoring_and_slo: Define SLIs: post-ranking end-to-end p95 latency (< 200ms target for 'latency-first' customers), error rate (< 0.5%), fallback rate (< 8% baseline)
New metrics: region_health_score (per-region), breaker_trip_count (per-tenant, per-region), fallback_chain_latency, quality_delta_mrr
Alerts: immediate (P0) alert if fallback rate increases by 3x baseline or region_health_score drops below 30 for >2 minutes
Dashboards: heatmap of region_health_score, breaker state timeline, top 10 tenants by breaker trips, fallback chain distribution
risks_and_mitigation: Quality regressions: introduce A/B tests that compare MRR/CTR of fallback chains; maintain an automatic rollback if degradation exceeds threshold
State sync complexity: persisted breaker states may lag; mitigation: conservative defaults, and short sync windows plus periodic reconciliation job
Operational complexity for customers: provide console view and per-tenant blueprint to tune fallback profile; default to conservative (quality-first) profile
Increased cost from cross-region routing: prefer local fallbacks first; expose cost impacts in tenant billing and provide 'cost-first' opt-in profile
